integration_questions: With the 0.016 m footprint, does the sum of readings at bend entries stay well above 0.05, and do line_loss_events fall below the 0.95 per run seen in iteration 4?
Does steering_oscillation stay near 0.2 on the oval, or does the larger footprint blur the signal enough to add jitter?
On the slalom, does progress move past the 0.17 to 0.18 plateau? If not, the limit is probably speed or turn rate rather than sensing.
Does the s-bend progress hold near 0.49 with the larger footprint, or does the blurred edge cost a bend the 0.012 m footprint handled?

intent: Test whether a larger sensor footprint (0.012 to 0.016 m) fixes the slalom plateau and the oval line-loss events. Relative to iteration 4, the only change is sensor_size. wheel_track returns to 0.09 m, the best s-bend value, after 0.08 m cut s-bend progress from 0.486 to 0.330. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.2, line_loss_events on the oval at or below 0.5 per run, and s-bend progress at or above 0.45, which together would beat the 404.6 score.
learning: Iteration 5 showed that wheel_track 0.08 m reduces s-bend progress (0.486 to 0.330) even though the oval still finishes 20 of 20, so 0.09 m is the better track width. Slalom progress has stayed at 0.16 to 0.18 across every design tested, so the next lever is sensing, not turn authority. If the footprint change lifts slalom progress, keep it and consider mass or wheel_radius next. If slalom stays flat, the limit is likely speed or controller-side, and the geometry work should move to wheel_radius and mass to add speed on the tight bends.
rationale: Five iterations of evidence point the same way. Iteration 4 (score 404.6, best so far) used the 5-sensor row at y=0.08 m, spanning ±0.03 m at 0.015 m pitch with 0.012 m footprints, and wheel_track 0.09 m. It finished 20 of 20 oval runs and gave s-bend progress 0.486. Iteration 5 narrowed wheel_track to 0.08 m with everything else unchanged, and scored lower (384.4). The oval stayed at 20 of 20 and its mean score rose slightly, but s-bend progress fell from 0.486 to 0.330 and line_loss_events rose to 1.0. So 0.08 m overshoots the turn-authority sweet spot on the s-bend, and I revert to 0.09 m. Slalom progress has sat at 0.16 to 0.18 across iterations 1, 3, 4 and 5, whatever the wheel track, sensor row position or array span. That makes the slalom stall look like a sensing problem rather than a turn-rate one. Two candidate causes fit: the 0.012 m footprint sees the 25 mm tape only partially at bend entries, and the oval still shows 0.95 line-loss events per run. Iteration 2 showed that widening the array to ±0.06 m hurts, so I leave span alone. I make one change relative to iteration 4: sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m, the largest allowed footprint. A larger footprint covers more of the 25 mm tape at each sensor, which should give a smoother, less dropout-prone signal at bend entries. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, slalom progress above the 0.18 plateau, and s-bend progress held at or near 0.49. The risk is that a larger footprint blurs the response to a sharp bend, so the s-bend could drop, and the Integrator should check that first.
